name: walk_node_chain_with_callbacks
description: Follows a chain of linked records, where the first word of each record holds the link to the next. For every record it calls a routine with the record's second word and then calls a routine on the record itself with the size value eight, stopping when the link is zero.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign and then decimal digits from a null-terminated string, accumulating the digits into an integer. Scanning stops at the first character that is not a digit, and the value is negated when a minus sign was present.

name: call_system_library_allocate
description: Calls the allocation entry of the system library through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_system_library_free
description: Calls the release entry of the system library through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_system_library_find_task
description: Calls the task lookup entry of the system library through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_system_library_close
description: Calls the library close entry of the system library through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_system_library_open
description: Calls the library open entry of the system library through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_rename_entry
description: Calls the rename entry of the second library, whose base is held in a global, through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_unlock_entry
description: Calls the unlock entry of the second library, whose base is held in a global, through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_duplicate_lock_entry
description: Calls the duplicate-lock entry of the second library, whose base is held in a global, through its jump vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor. For divisors above 16 bits it runs a bit-by-bit restoring division, otherwise it performs two 16-bit divisions, and it returns the quotient and remainder together as a pair.

name: multiply_32bit_low_result
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from the data registers using 16-bit partial products and keeps the low 32 bits. It returns that product together with a half-swapped copy of the second operand.

name: call_and_negate_on_flag
description: Calls a routine and returns its first result, negated when a second value returned by that routine is nonzero.

name: validate_disk_bitmap_words
description: Writes a two-digit count into a status buffer, then walks a range of bitmap words and compares each bit against a stored copy. Mismatches are counted and reported through library routines before the walk continues.

name: copy_memory_then_dispatch
description: Calls the system memory copy routine through the library vector, then transfers control through a target taken from a computed table.

name: clear_blitter_task_word
description: Runs a sequence of library calls and a base-address routine, then reads a pointer from the task structure. If the word at that pointer matches a fixed pattern, it saves the word and overwrites it with zero, clearing the shared cell.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter one step at a time until it wraps to minus one, then returns. It is a busy wait with no output.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: This entry decodes only as invalid instruction data, so it is a stub with no behaviour.

name: clear_cpu_task_word
description: Runs a sequence of library calls and a base-address routine, then reads a pointer from the task structure. If the word at that pointer matches a fixed pattern, it saves the word and overwrites it with zero, clearing the shared cell.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter one step at a time until it wraps to minus one, then returns. It is a busy wait with no output.

name: clear_main_task_word
description: Runs a sequence of library calls and a base-address routine, then reads a pointer from the task structure. If the word at that pointer matches a fixed pattern, it saves the word and overwrites it with zero, clearing the shared cell.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter one step at a time until it wraps to minus one, then returns. It is a busy wait with no output.

name: copy_words_then_flush_cache
description: Runs a loop four times that calls a bit-stream routine and copies words from one buffer into another, then flushes the processor caches through the system library when a global counter exceeds thirty-six.

name: unpack_backward_bitstream
description: Unpacks a compressed block by reading control bits from the end of the input and copying literal bytes backward into the output, with run lengths decoded from the bit stream.

name: decode_backward_packed_block
description: Decodes a packed block by reading bits from the end of the input and copying bytes backward into the output, using a table of length codes to size each copy run.

name: unpack_backward_literal_runs
description: Copies literal bytes backward from the end of the input, four bytes per pass, with run lengths decoded from the bit stream deciding how many bytes each run copies before the loop ends.

name: clear_install_task_word
description: Runs a sequence of library calls and a base-address routine, then reads a pointer from the task structure. If the word at that pointer matches a fixed pattern, it saves the word and overwrites it with zero, clearing the shared cell.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter one step at a time until it wraps to minus one, then returns. It is a busy wait with no output.

name: copy_words_then_flush_cache
description: Runs a loop three times that calls a bit-stream routine and copies words from one buffer into another, then flushes the processor caches through the system library when a global counter exceeds thirty-six.

name: unpack_backward_bitstream
description: Unpacks a compressed block by reading control bits from the end of the input and copying literal bytes backward into the output, with run lengths decoded from the bit stream.

name: decode_backward_packed_block
description: Decodes a packed block by reading bits from the end of the input and copying bytes backward into the output, using a table of length codes to size each copy run.

name: unpack_backward_literal_runs
description: Copies literal bytes backward from the end of the input, four bytes per pass, with run lengths decoded from the bit stream deciding how many bytes each run copies before the loop ends.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: This entry decodes only as invalid instruction data, so it is a stub with no behaviour.

name: invoke_library_routine
description: Calls one library routine through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing. Only this single library call is described by the evidence.

name: run_task_guarded_setup
description: Brackets a sequence of library calls with a task forbid and permit pair, looking up the current task and freeing or allocating memory, then stores a status value in a global and returns it.

name: allocate_and_open_checked_handle
description: Gets a value from a routine, allocates a block through the system library and calls the open entry of the second library, comparing returned values. On a match it closes what it opened and releases the task lock before returning.

name: examine_locked_object_field
description: Locks an object through the second library and examines it. If both steps succeed it returns one 32-bit field of the examination record, otherwise zero, and the lock is released before returning.

name: dispatch_table_entry_by_index
description: Looks up an index through a library call. If the index is zero it releases the lock and returns minus one; otherwise it calls the routine stored at that index in a table, releases the lock, and returns its result.

name: open_then_close_file
description: Opens a file through the second library and, if the open succeeds, stores the handle in a global, calls three routines and closes the handle.

name: open_show_error_then_close
description: Opens a file through the second library and, if the open succeeds, calls a sequence of routines. For a status value of two or three it shows a German error message from the data, then closes the file.

name: write_while_data_pending
description: Calls the write entry of the second library in a loop that repeats while a check routine reports more data, and calls a routine after each write.

name: write_if_check_passes
description: Calls the write entry of the second library once, but only when a check routine returns a nonzero value.

name: find_word_in_terminated_table
description: Scans a table of 16-bit entries that ends with a minus-one marker, stepping forward by the length of each entry, until it finds an entry equal to the value in the data register. It leaves the search position in the address register.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the characters of a null-terminated string addressed by the address register and returns the count in the data register.

name: wait_blitter_then_spin
description: Clears a state word and, when a flag bit is set, waits until the blitter is idle, installs a routine as the interrupt handler pointer and then loops forever. It uses the blitter and DMA control registers.

name: store_constant_status_value
description: Stores the constant sixty-four into a global status cell and returns.

name: probe_floppy_drive_entry
description: When a state cell is zero, it attempts a lock through the second library and records whether a returned status equals a fixed code. Otherwise it looks up a device entry, checks that its name begins with the letters D and F followed by a digit from zero to three, sets the state cell and releases the lock.

name: parse_unit_number_after_prefix
description: Compares the input string against a fixed prefix stored in the program. When the prefix matches, it reads the character that follows; if that character is a digit it stores its value, otherwise it stores the all-ones value.

name: set_flag_if_field_zero
description: Sets a global flag to minus one when a field of the structure it reads is zero, and to zero otherwise.

name: wait_for_port_message
description: Waits on a message port, takes the message from it through the system library, and calls the enable routine of the library when a field of that message is nonzero.

name: release_forbid_and_reply
description: When a message pointer is set, forbids task switching, replies to the message through the system library and clears the pointer.

name: open_library_and_read_version
description: Opens libraries through the system open entry, storing each returned base in a global, and finally reads the 16-bit version field of the last base into the global.

name: close_held_libraries
description: Closes the library whose base is held in a global through the system close entry, once for each of three checks that find the global nonzero.

name: call_entry_and_store_flag
description: Calls a library entry through its vector and stores minus one in a global when the call returns nonzero, and zero otherwise.

name: step_to_parent_if_flagged
description: When a flag in a global is set, calls the parent-directory entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: setup_shared_record_state
description: When a flag is clear, allocates memory and runs several system library calls, exchanges a field of a shared record with a saved value, and when a lookup succeeds, does the same for a second record. It then sets the flag to minus one.

name: clear_shared_record_entry
description: When a flag is set, stores a value in a shared record, looks up and closes an entry through the second library, calls two more library entries and then clears the flag.

name: store_current_task_pointer
description: Calls the task lookup entry of the system library and stores the returned task pointer in a global.

name: store_adjusted_char_then_call
description: When a flag is clear, stores the character at the input pointer plus sixty-four into a fixed byte cell and calls a routine. Otherwise it only calls that routine.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies characters from the source pointer to the destination pointer, one at a time, until a zero byte has been copied.

name: set_flag_if_field_below
description: Sets a global flag to minus one when a 16-bit field of a record, reduced by thirty-six, is negative, and to zero otherwise.

name: setup_device_io_request
description: When a flag is clear, allocates a signal through the system library and, if that succeeds, opens a device and sends a prepared I/O request whose fields are set beforehand. It releases the signal and closes the device on the failure paths.

name: clear_flag_after_library_call
description: When a flag is set, calls a library entry and then clears the flag.

name: try_lock_with_fallback
description: When a flag is clear, temporarily sets a field of a shared record to minus one, attempts a lock through the second library and restores the field. It then calls a library entry when the lock fails, or unlocks when it succeeds.

name: invoke_fallback_library_entry
description: Calls one library entry through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: configure_port_when_ready
description: When a 16-bit field minus thirty-nine is nonnegative, calls a library entry. If that returns zero, it calls the library again with a new value, then makes two more library calls and sets the global to 255.

name: clear_flag_after_library_calls
description: When a flag is set, calls a library entry and, if it returns zero, calls two more library entries and clears the flag.

name: set_flag_and_enter_supervisor
description: Sets a global to minus one when bit one of a status byte is set, and to zero otherwise, then enters supervisor state through the system library.

name: read_vector_base_register
description: Copies the processor's vector base register into a global. When a flag is clear, that value is replaced with zero first.

name: run_status_gated_library_call
description: Calls a routine, calls a library entry only when a status bit of a record is set, and then runs one of two alternative paths depending on the result of a second library call.

name: run_install_menu
description: Shows the installation menu with options to install the game on the hard disk, create a save-state disk, view the troubleshooting document or quit. It then dispatches to the copy and assign steps for the chosen option.

name: dispatch_ram_command_lines
description: Loops over command dispatch steps that refer to the game's command files in RAM, such as Copy, Format, Install, More and Run, and branches on a character code read from a line buffer.

name: prompt_and_install_to_path
description: Prompts for a destination path, checks it with lock and examine calls, and copies the game files from the install disk, with German status messages shown during the copy.

name: read_single_input_into_buffer
description: Reserves a ten-byte stack buffer and passes it with a count of one to a routine that takes the global handle, returning nothing.

name: copy_string_up_to_limit
description: Formats a string into a 100-byte stack buffer, then copies it to the destination. When the string is longer than the limit it copies only the limit and writes a terminating zero after it.

name: store_table_entry_and_dispatch
description: Copies one word from a table, indexed by a register, into a fixed field. It then calls a routine with two record fields and the value that routine returns, and calls a second routine with a record field, a global buffer and the value one.

name: run_copy_command
description: Formats a copy command line from two text arguments into a 200-byte buffer and runs it through the system execute entry. When execution fails it shows a German message that the copy command could not be started and waits briefly.

name: prompt_until_yes_or_no
description: Repeats a prompt and reads a character until it is a J or an N, then returns the character read.

name: create_directory_then_unlock
description: Calls the directory creation step with its argument and, when that returns a lock handle, releases the lock through the second library.

name: generate_save_directories
description: Shows a German status message that save directories are being generated, then creates eleven directories with names built from a two-digit suffix, releasing each lock after creation.

name: generate_save_file
description: Shows a German status message that a save file is being generated, opens a file, copies two names into a buffer, and then writes or removes data with a fixed block size depending on a check.

name: read_file_size_by_lock
description: Allocates a 260-byte info block, locks the given path in shared mode, examines it into the block and returns the 32-bit size field of the block. It returns zero when any step fails.

name: copy_file_with_error_messages
description: Checks that a source file exists and can be read and that the destination can be written, then copies the file. A missing, unreadable or unwritable file produces its own German error message.

name: check_install_disk_drive
description: Checks the install folder and the install program on the disk. When a flag is set, it locks a named entry and clears the flag if the entry is a floppy drive name from DF0 to DF3, then releases the lock.

name: set_flag_if_field_above
description: Sets a global flag to one when a 16-bit field of a record is greater than thirty-five, and to zero otherwise.

name: test_lock_and_release
description: Attempts to lock a named path through the second library, releases the lock if one was obtained, and returns whether the lock succeeded.

name: build_full_path_upwards
description: Walks upward through the parent directories of the current directory, reading each directory name into a path buffer with slash separators. When the root is reached it ends the path with a colon.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination, including the terminating zero, and returns the destination pointer.

name: compute_string_length
description: Walks a zero-terminated string and returns the number of characters before the terminator. It does not modify memory.

name: convert_char_to_uppercase
description: Returns the input character converted to uppercase when it is a lowercase letter, and unchanged otherwise.

name: convert_char_to_lowercase
description: Returns the input character converted to lowercase when it is an uppercase letter, and unchanged otherwise.

name: run_formatted_print
description: Clears a status global and passes its argument and the caller's stack argument list to the formatted output routine.

name: select_stream_handle
description: When the argument is zero, stores either the value a routine returns for a fixed stream, or minus one when a status bit is set. Otherwise it passes the stored value and the fixed stream to that routine, and returns the global.

name: format_printf_style_text
description: Walks a format string, copying literal characters through a character output routine and expanding each percent specifier. It handles flags, widths and an asterisk width taken from the arguments, and returns zero or minus one.

name: skip_whitespace_then_peek
description: Reads characters through the stream routine until one is not in the space class, then pushes it back. It returns zero, or minus one when the stream reports the end of input.

name: scan_signed_integer_in_base
description: Reads an optional sign and then digits of a given base through the stream routine, accumulating the value by digit position and storing the signed result. An x prefix is accepted for base sixteen. It returns the number of characters consumed.

name: read_nonzero_char_with_eot
description: Reads characters until a nonzero result, returning minus one at end of input. A value of four marks end of text: it backs the position up by one, sets an error flag bit and returns minus one.

name: read_buffered_byte
description: Returns the next byte of a buffer when the read position is before the end, advancing the position. Otherwise it calls the refill routine and returns its result.

name: refill_buffer_and_read_byte
description: Refills a read buffer through a block read routine when it is empty, closes flagged entries when a flag is set, sets an end or error flag from the result, and returns the next byte or minus one.

name: write_char_to_buffer
description: Stores one character at the write position of a buffer and advances it, returning the character. It returns minus one when the input is minus one or the buffer has no room.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for a given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or null when the terminator is reached first.

name: read_file_slot_with_error
description: Checks that a file slot index is valid and that the slot is open for reading, setting an error code and returning minus one otherwise. It then calls the read routine for the slot's handle and records the I/O error when that read fails.

name: return_immediately
description: Returns at once without doing any work.

name: create_tagged_context_block
description: Allocates a context block sized as six times a global count, initializes its header fields, stamps a four-letter tag into it and links it to the current process record. An allocation failure returns without linking.

name: build_command_line_arguments
description: Allocates a buffer for a command line, copies the command name and the given text into it, skips whitespace and splits the remaining text into arguments, each terminated with a zero byte.

name: append_string_bounded
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying at most 32766 characters, and terminates the result.

name: append_counted_string
description: Appends up to a given number of characters from a source string to the end of a destination, stopping at the source terminator. It writes a terminator after the appended text when the source was not exhausted, and returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_string_with_zero_padding
description: Copies characters from a source string to a destination for up to a given count, stopping at the source terminator, then fills the remaining positions with zero bytes. It returns the destination pointer.

name: setup_icon_window_record
description: Opens the icon library and looks up entries by name, storing the found pointer and two values in the window record it receives, then releases what it locked.

name: call_and_clear_first_byte
description: Stores the buffer pointer in a global, calls a routine with that value and a fixed stack argument, then clears the first byte of the buffer and returns the routine's result.

name: call_and_clear_first_byte
description: Stores the buffer pointer in a global, calls a routine with that value and a fixed stack argument, then clears the first byte of the buffer and returns the routine's result.

name: store_char_and_advance
description: Writes one byte to the output pointer held in a global, advances that pointer and returns the byte.

name: call_with_stack_arguments
description: Passes its argument and the caller's stack argument list to a routine, with no return value.

name: write_digits_backward
description: Writes the digits of a number backward into a buffer from the end, using a digit table, and prepends a minus sign when the value is negative.

name: format_conversion_with_padding
description: Processes a format string, copying literal characters through a character output routine and expanding each conversion specification with its sign, zero fill and width. It returns the count of characters written, or minus one on failure.

name: perform_signed_division
description: Calls a division routine on its operands and negates the quotient when exactly one operand is negative. It returns the quotient together with the second operand register.

name: call_and_return_register_pair
description: Calls a routine and returns a pair built from the data register it was given and the register value the call left behind.

name: self_call_and_return
description: Calls a routine with no arguments and then returns. The routine it calls is the one that contains this call, so it does nothing beyond that call.

name: unsigned_divide_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor. For divisors above 16 bits it runs a bit-by-bit restoring division, otherwise it performs two 16-bit divisions. It returns the remainder and quotient together.

name: call_with_fixed_buffer
description: Calls a routine with its argument and a fixed buffer address, and returns nothing.

name: output_char_flushing_newline
description: Passes its character and stream to an output routine. When the character is a newline and a flag bit of the stream is set, it also calls a flush routine with minus one.

name: store_char_in_buffer
description: Stores one character into a buffer while there is room, advances the position and returns the character. When the buffer is full it calls an overflow routine instead.

name: process_each_22byte_record
description: Walks a table of 22-byte records up to a fixed end address and calls a routine on each record, returning nothing.

name: release_record_resources
description: Releases the resources a record holds according to its flag bits, returns the accumulated status, or minus one for a null record, and zeroes the record's fields.

name: release_record_flagged_resources
description: Releases the resources a record holds according to its flag bits, returns the accumulated status, and zeroes the record's fields.

name: write_char_to_stream
description: Returns minus one when the stream is in an error state. Otherwise it stores the character in the stream buffer when one is in use, or writes it directly through the write routine, and returns the character.

name: allocate_free_record_slot
description: Scans a table of 22-byte records for one whose in-use flag is clear, clears its fields and returns it, or null when every record is in use.

name: find_free_record_from
description: Scans forward from the given record for one whose in-use flag is clear, clears it and returns it, or null at the end of the table.

name: clear_record_fields
description: Zeroes the three words at the start of the record addressed by the address register.

name: allocate_record_buffer
description: Allocates a 1024-byte buffer for a record. When allocation fails it uses a buffer built into the record and sets its size to one; when it succeeds it sets a flag and a follow-up routine may set a second flag.

name: free_linked_node_list
description: Walks a singly linked list from the global head, releasing each node through a memory routine with a size equal to the node's stored size plus eight, then clears the head.

name: free_node_chain_from_argument
description: Walks a linked chain starting at the address register, releasing each node through a memory routine with a size equal to its stored size plus eight, and clears the global head when done.

name: push_node_onto_list
description: Allocates a node sized from the argument plus eight, links it at the front of the global list with the given owner, and returns a pointer past the link words. It returns null when allocation fails.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its argument to a routine and returns nothing.

name: remove_node_from_list
description: Searches the global list for the node whose data pointer matches the argument, unlinks it and releases it through a memory routine. It returns zero when a node is removed and minus one when none matches.

name: remove_node_matching_owner
description: Searches a chain for the node that belongs to the owner structure passed in, unlinks it and releases it. It returns zero when a node was removed and minus one when none matched.

name: unlink_node_and_release
description: Unlinks the node in the address registers from the chain, updating the head when the node is first, and releases it through the memory routine.

name: set_list_head_from_pointer
description: Stores the value read from the address register into the global list head, then calls a routine and returns zero.

name: check_file_slot_interactive
description: Checks that a file slot index is valid and occupied, setting an error code and returning minus one otherwise. For a valid slot it returns one when the slot's handle is interactive, and zero when it is not.

name: delete_file_with_error
description: Deletes a file through the second library and returns zero when it succeeds. On failure it records the I/O error in a global and returns minus one.

name: return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any work.

name: write_file_slot_with_error
description: Checks that a file slot index is valid and open for writing, setting an error code and returning minus one otherwise. It calls the write routine for the slot's handle and records the I/O error when that write fails.

name: check_break_signal
description: Checks the task's signal bits for the break signal. When it is set and no handler is installed, it returns the signal bits; when a handler is installed it calls the handler and returns zero.

name: write_global_word_block
description: Passes a four-byte global cell to a write routine along with the output handle, then calls a routine with the value one, returning nothing.

name: call_optional_hook_then_routine
description: Calls an optional hook routine when one is installed, then passes its argument to another routine and returns nothing.

name: release_global_record_resources
description: Releases a group of resources held in a global record: it frees each sized entry in a loop, calls the optional hook, unlocks and drops the lock entries, then frees the record itself.

name: return_immediately
description: Returns at once without doing any work.

name: close_file_slot
description: Checks that a file slot index is valid and in use, closing its handle through the second library unless the slot is marked as preserved, then clears the slot and returns zero. An invalid slot sets an error code and returns minus one.

name: multiply_32bit_partial_sum
description: Forms the cross products of the 16-bit halves of two 32-bit data registers and returns their sum shifted into the high word, together with the second operand register.

name: close_file_handle
description: Calls the close entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: call_current_directory_entry
description: Calls the current-directory entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: delete_file_entry
description: Calls the delete-file entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: fetch_io_error_code
description: Calls the I/O error entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: open_file_entry
description: Calls the open entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: read_file_entry
description: Calls the read entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: write_file_entry
description: Calls the write entry of the second library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: close_system_library_entry
description: Calls the library close entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: close_system_library_entry
description: Calls the library close entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: allocate_memory_entry
description: Calls the memory allocation entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: allocate_memory_entry
description: Calls the memory allocation entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: find_task_entry
description: Calls the task lookup entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: find_task_entry
description: Calls the task lookup entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: forbid_task_switching
description: Calls the forbid entry of the system library, which stops task switching, and returns nothing.

name: free_memory_entry
description: Calls the memory release entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: free_memory_entry
description: Calls the memory release entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: get_message_from_port
description: Calls the get-message entry of the system library through its vector to take a message from a port, and returns nothing.

name: open_system_library_entry
description: Calls the library open entry of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: invoke_system_library_routine
description: Calls a routine of the system library through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing.

name: wait_on_message_port

name: duplicate_lock_entry

name: unlock_entry

name: invoke_library_routine_once
description: Calls one library routine through its vector, with no arguments set here, and returns nothing. Only this single library call is described by the evidence.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call

name: fill_table_from_max_entry

name: allocate_message_and_open_dos
description: Allocates a message structure through the system library, reads the current task and the current directory, opens the dos library and waits for a reply message. It returns twenty when the allocation fails.

name: reply_and_release_message
description: Finds the current task and exchanges its stored message pointer with the argument. It closes a library when the saved entry is nonzero, and when a second saved entry is set it forbids task switching and replies to the message. It then frees a block and returns the previous message pointer.

name: sum_memory_region_sizes
description: Walks a list of memory-region entries and sums the sizes of those whose attribute bits match the mask passed in.

name: print_memory_usage_table
description: Parses a memory type selector from the command arguments, queries the available, in-use, maximum and largest memory figures through the system library, and prints a table with the headings Type, Available, In-Use, Maximum and Largest.

name: call_with_stack_slot_pointer
description: Passes its two arguments and a pointer to a fixed stack slot to a routine, returning nothing.

name: format_and_emit_stack_text
